newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS/IBM calls ahead of earnings.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS/IBM calls ahead of earnings.

text.p: Call options on International Business Machines Corp traded heavily ahead of the firm's second quarter earnings due out after the market close, traders said.

They noted that interest in call options far outpaced puts, despite a pullback in the stock today and a sharp downturn in the market late last week after Microsoft Corp's earnings report, which had met analysts' projections but yet disappointed the Street.
"It seems like all the momentum players are in IBM," said Michael Schwartz, a managing director of Oppenheimer & Co.
"Not even Intel (Intel Corp ) options have volume close to IBM," he noted. "They've temporarily deserted Intel."

IBM August 105 and 110 options were the busiest options on the Chicago Board Options Exchange with more than 9,200 and 6,900 contracts respectively changing hands by mid-afternoon in an otherwise relatively quiet post-expiration market.
On the puts side, August 100 and 95 puts traded about 3,000 contracts each.
IBM stock, which had risen about four points on Friday despite a selloff in the rest of the market, was off 6/16 at 103-13/16.
Bernie Schaeffer, head of Cincinnati-based Investment Research Institute, noted that accumulation of speculative call positions was a bearish signal for the IBM stock.
"IBM is thus extremely vulnerable to the downside, should earnings prove to be less than a 'blowout'," he said.
Jack Callahan, an independent market maker at CBOE, agreed.
"Upside surprises, the market isn't surprised any more," he said. "Downside is where surprises are."
Still, Schwartz said it was too early to declare an end to the market's bull run led by blue-chip technology stocks.
Although the market tumbled on Friday and was hit by followthrough selling early Monday, it remained relatively resilient, he said.
"If I didn't see these high-tech names there (on the most active options list), I'd say that we're close to a negative reaction," he added.

The volatility curve for IBM options was inverted as most of the interest was short-term and focused on August options. IBM August 105 puts and calls had implied volatilities of around 55 percent, against September's 45 percent and the stock's one-month actual volatility of 30 percent.
Shorter-dated at-the-money options have higher gamma, which provides quicker premium acceleration against stock price movements, although they are vulnerable to time decay.

But since July options matured just last week, the front-month options have a fairly long life to expiration, giving short-term speculators not as much gamma as they had received for last week's Microsoft play, traders said.
According to First Call, the consensus estimate for IBM earnings wqw $1.42, in a range from $1.36 to $1.50, against $1.26 a year earlier.
-- Shin Kishima/Chicago Derivatives Desk ((312-408-8750))
